      #45 - Self-Service Application Portal — Full Automation

      What & Why

      The current portal requires manual admin action at every step. That is not acceptable for a patent promotion product operating at the level of Amazon or Walmart supplier onboarding. This task builds the complete self-service layer: applicants apply, pay, get confirmed, and access their workspace without a single manual step from the owner. The owner's role becomes oversight and exception-handling — not order-taking.

      Done looks like

      For a factory applicant:

      1. They land on the public site, click "Apply as Factory Partner"
      2. They fill a structured application form: company name, registration number, country, production capacity, CNC capabilities, contact details
      3. They accept the NDA (shown inline with the form, not a separate step)
      4. They pay the access fee via Paystack — hosted checkout, ZAR amount shown with live exchange rate
      5. On payment confirmation they receive an automated email: "Application received — under review"
      6. Admin reviews and approves in BoxPanel (one click)
      7. Applicant receives approval email with direct vault link — they sign in and land in the Factory Workspace
      8. Zero phone calls. Zero manual emails. Zero spreadsheets.

      For a licensee applicant:

      • Same flow, different form fields (company, country, intended use, distribution territory)
      • Access tier is Licensee Workspace on approval

      For an attorney:

      • Same flow, different form fields (bar association, jurisdiction, firm name, matter reference)
      • Access tier is Attorney Workspace on approval

      For the owner:

      • BoxPanel shows live pipeline: Applied → Paid → Under Review → Approved/Declined
      • One-click approve or decline with reason
      • Full applicant detail visible at each stage
      • No manual data entry ever needed

      Out of scope

      • Automated approval without admin review (the owner retains final approval authority)
      • Bulk import of existing contacts
      • API access / partner API keys (future phase)

      Steps

      1. Public application landing page — Add a dedicated /apply route with three persona cards (Factory / Licensee / Attorney). Each card shows what access includes and what is required to apply. This is public — no sign-in needed to view it.
      2. Structured application form per persona — Three form variants under /apply/factory, /apply/licensee, /apply/attorney. Each collects all mandatory fields for that persona. Clerk sign-up is embedded inline (or triggered on submit for new users) so the applicant's Clerk account is created as part of the flow.
      3. Inline NDA acceptance — The NDA text is displayed at the bottom of the application form with a checkbox. On submit, POST /nda/accept is called server-side. No separate modal step.
      4. Payment step — After form submission, the applicant is redirected to the Paystack hosted payment page. On return, /payments/verify is called automatically (no manual user action).
      5. Application pipeline view in BoxPanel — Add a pipeline column view (not just a flat list) to BoxPanel showing applicants bucketed by stage: Applied / Paid-Awaiting-Review / Approved / Declined. Each card shows persona, company, country, days in current stage.
      6. Persona workspace auto-routing on approval — When an applicant is approved, the system reads their role field and the approval email deep-links directly to their persona workspace (/workspace/factories, /workspace/licensees, /workspace/attorneys). Sign in → correct workspace. No manual navigation.
      7. Profile pre-fill from application — All fields collected in the application form are written to user_access_allowlist at submission time. profileCompletedAt is set on form submit (not as a separate step after approval). The applicant never fills in their details twice.

      Relevant files

      • artifacts/block-box-patent/src/App.tsx
      • artifacts/block-box-patent/src/pages/BoxPanel.tsx
      • artifacts/block-box-patent/src/components/AuthNdaGate.tsx
      • artifacts/api-server/src/routes/nda.ts
      • artifacts/api-server/src/routes/payments.ts
      • artifacts/api-server/src/routes/admin.ts

      BlockBox EPS Cornice System — Independent Packaging Waste Audit Brief

      Document type: Audit Scope of Work — Third-Party Packaging Waste Verification
      Prepared by: Block Box (Pty) Ltd
      Date: 15 July 2026
      Version: 1.0
      Intended recipient: Accredited packaging / environmental auditor (e.g., Intertek, Bureau Veritas, SGS, or equivalent body accredited under ISO/IEC 17020 or ISO/IEC 17065)
      Classification: Commercial — Confidential

      Purpose

      Block Box (Pty) Ltd manufactures EPS (expanded polystyrene) cornice profiles using a patented hot-wire CNC block-cutting system. The company's ESG Export Brief (version 1.0, 15 July 2026) discloses that certain waste-elimination figures — specifically the plastic tubing, cardboard box, and label quantities eliminated per block relative to a legacy competitor system — are projections derived from supplier market research, not the result of an independent third-party audit.

      This document constitutes the scope of work for an accredited third-party auditor to verify those figures and issue a signed auditor's statement (Annex A of the ESG Export Brief) that UK, EU, and Australian procurement departments may rely upon in their own EPR, PPWR, or APCO compliance filings.

      1. Background — The BlockBox Packaging System

      1.1 System overview

      BlockBox cornices are cut by a CNC hot-wire machine from solid EPS blocks (grade 20DV, dimensions 595 mm × 315 mm × 2 000 mm, sourced from Isowall Group, South Africa). The cutting G-code is designed so that a 10 mm solid EPS edge remains uncut on both sides of the block, keeping all finished cornice profiles structurally connected within the block until the point of customer extraction at retail.

      Consequence for packaging: No secondary material — no plastic tubing, no cardboard box, no adhesive label — is applied to individual cornice units at any stage of manufacture, storage, wholesale, or retail display. The block itself serves as the packaging. The sole packaging material in the supply chain is standard agricultural PE pallet shrink-wrap applied at the dispatch point in South Africa.

      1.2 Primary source documents provided to auditor

      The following documents are provided as part of this audit brief and constitute the complete evidential basis for the figures to be verified:

      DocumentVersion / DatePurpose
      EPS Cornice Block Optimization — Executive Summary & Cost Analysis24 February 2026Internal technical record; source of block dimensions, unit counts per block, packaging labor and material savings per block
      BlockBox 1.5 m EPS Cornice — Global Market Research Report v2.015 July 2026Source of legacy competitor packaging quantities and aggregate waste-elimination figures
      BlockBox EPS Cornice System — Export ESG Brief v1.015 July 2026The document this audit will support; contains the figures requiring verification
      South African Provisional Patent ApplicationOn fileTechnical description of the block-cutting and block-packaging system
      Isowall Group Quote Q-10742On fileSupplier confirmation of EPS block specification (595 × 315 mm, grade 20DV)

      2. Audit Scope

      The audit comprises three verification components, each of which must be addressed in the auditor's output report:

      Component A — BlockBox Production Process Verification

      Objective: Confirm that the BlockBox manufacturing process, as described in the source documents listed above and as observed at the production facility, results in zero secondary packaging material (plastic tubing, cardboard boxes, adhesive labels) being applied to individual cornice units at any stage prior to dispatch.

      Verification activities:

      1. Facility visit to the BlockBox production site (South Africa).
      2. Direct observation of at least one complete production run from raw EPS block receipt through to palletised dispatch — covering CNC hot-wire cutting, block removal, pallet stacking, and shrink-wrap application.
      3. Confirmation that no individual unit wrapping, boxing, or labelling station exists in the production workflow.
      4. Inspection of dispatch records for at least three consecutive dispatch batches to confirm that the sole packaging material recorded is pallet shrink-wrap.
      5. Review of the G-code cutting program to confirm the 10 mm uncut edge specification that maintains block connectivity (reference: EPS Block Optimization Executive Summary §6.3 and §2.2).

      Expected auditor finding: A signed statement that the auditor observed the production process and confirms: (a) no secondary packaging material is applied to individual cornice units; and (b) the pallet shrink-wrap is the only packaging material present at point of dispatch.

      Component B — Waste Elimination Quantity Verification

      Objective: Verify the waste elimination quantities published in the ESG Export Brief (Section 2.2) against a named legacy benchmark.

      Figures to be verified:

      MetricClaimed figureSource in ESG Brief
      Plastic tubing / wrapping eliminated per block≈ 49 m§2.2
      Plastic tubing / wrapping eliminated per 10 000 blocks≈ 490 000 m§2.2
      Cardboard boxes eliminated per block≈ 1.7 boxes§2.2
      Cardboard boxes eliminated per 10 000 blocks≈ 17 000 boxes§2.2
      Adhesive labels eliminated per block≈ 23.2 labels§2.2
      Adhesive labels eliminated per 10 000 blocks≈ 232 000 labels§2.2
      Secondary packaging waste reduction vs legacy94 %Executive Summary, §1

      Named legacy benchmark: The legacy comparison system is standard EPS cornice packaging as used by Turkish and Chinese origin manufacturers and distributed through South African wholesale channels — specifically the individual-unit packaging format comprising: (a) a polyethylene sleeve or tube per cornice piece; (b) a cardboard box per batch of cornice pieces; (c) an adhesive barcode/product label per piece and per box. The BlockBox 1.5 m Global Market Research Report v2.0 §4 (competitive landscape) and §5.2 (packaging cost breakdown) describe this benchmark. Supplier evidence (Sunny Packs wholesale price list, as cited in the Market Research Report §5.2) is provided to the auditor as a supplementary input.

      Verification activities:

      1. Obtain the packaging specification for a named legacy EPS cornice product line of comparable profile dimensions (110 mm or 140 mm profile; 2 m or 1.5 m length) from at least one of the following: a wholesale packaging supplier, a named competitor's product data sheet, or a logistics industry standard for individually wrapped EPS cornice.
      2. Record the following measurable quantities for the named legacy product:
        • Length of plastic sleeve / tube per individual cornice piece (metres)
        • Number of pieces packed per cardboard box
        • Number of adhesive labels applied per piece and per box
      3. Multiply the per-unit figures by the number of units per BlockBox block (110 mm profile: 140 units per 595 × 315 × 2 000 mm block; 140 mm profile: 112 units per block — reference: EPS Block Optimization Executive Summary §4.2) to derive the total legacy packaging eliminated per block.
      4. Compare derived figures to the claimed figures in the ESG Brief §2.2 and confirm whether the projected quantities are within a reasonable range (defined as ± 20 % of the auditor's independently derived figure, given the variability in legacy packaging formats across suppliers).
      5. State whether the auditor considers the claimed figures to be materially accurate, materially overstated, or materially understated relative to the named benchmark.

      Expected auditor finding: A signed statement that identifies: (a) the named legacy product / supplier used as the benchmark; (b) the auditor's independently derived per-unit and per-block packaging quantities for that benchmark; (c) a comparison to the claimed figures; and (d) a conclusion as to whether the ESG Brief's waste elimination claims are materially supported.

      Component C — Mono-Material Status Confirmation

      Objective: Confirm that the finished BlockBox cornice unit as supplied to retail contains no secondary materials, coatings, adhesives, composite elements, or embedded non-EPS components.

      Verification activities:

      1. Obtain a representative sample of finished BlockBox cornice units from at least one production batch (minimum 5 units from different positions within the block).
      2. Conduct a visual and physical inspection of each sample unit to confirm:
        • No adhesive or coating has been applied to the surface
        • No label, film, sleeve, or wrapper is attached to the unit
        • No composite insert or mechanical connector is embedded in the unit
      3. Confirm that the EPS material used is grade 20DV (density ≈ 20 kg/m³) as stated in the source documents, by reference to the Isowall Group supply specification or equivalent material test certificate.
      4. Record the resin identification code applicable to the material (expected: #6 PS — polystyrene) to confirm single-stream recyclability in principle.

      Expected auditor finding: A signed statement confirming: (a) the sample units inspected consist of a single EPS material with no secondary materials, coatings, or composite elements; (b) the material grade matches the stated specification; and (c) the product presents no technical barrier to single-stream recycling where EPS infrastructure is available.

      3. Deliverable — Auditor's Statement

      The auditor's output is a formal signed statement ("Auditor's Statement — BlockBox Packaging Waste Verification") to be appended to the ESG Export Brief as Annex A.

      The statement must:

      1. Identify the auditing organisation, the lead auditor's name and professional accreditation, and the date of issue.
      2. State the scope of work performed, referencing this brief by title, date, and version.
      3. Address each of the three verification components (A, B, C) with a clear finding — confirmed, confirmed with qualifications, or unable to confirm (with reasons).
      4. Confirm the specific figures it verifies or the range within which those figures are supported, so that a buyer can cite the auditor's statement directly in their own EPR, PPWR, or APCO filing.
      5. Be signed by the lead auditor and countersigned by a second reviewer within the auditing organisation.
      6. Bear the auditing organisation's official stamp or letterhead.

      Recommended statement structure

      AUDITOR'S STATEMENT — BLOCKBOX PACKAGING WASTE VERIFICATION
       
      Issued by:        [Auditing organisation name and accreditation number]
      Lead auditor:     [Name], [Professional designation]

      Scope reference:  BlockBox Packaging Waste Audit Brief, v1.0, 15 July 2026

      qualification that the BlockBox production process as observed on [date] at
      [facility address] results in zero secondary packaging material being applied
      to individual cornice units at any stage prior to dispatch. The sole packaging
      material present at dispatch is pallet shrink-wrap.]
       
      COMPONENT B — WASTE ELIMINATION QUANTITIES
       
      [Finding: We have independently verified the legacy benchmark packaging
      quantities using [named supplier / product line]. Our verification yields the
      following per-block legacy packaging quantities: plastic tubing [X m/block],
      cardboard boxes [Y boxes/block], adhesive labels [Z labels/block]. These
      figures are / are not within 20 % of the figures claimed in the ESG Export
      Brief §2.2. We consider the claimed waste elimination figures to be materially

      COMPONENT C — MONO-MATERIAL STATUS

      4. Auditor Qualification Requirements

      The auditing organisation must meet the following minimum requirements:

      RequirementSpecification
      AccreditationAccredited under ISO/IEC 17020 (inspection bodies) or ISO/IEC 17065 (product certification bodies) by a nationally recognised accreditation body (e.g., SANAS in South Africa, UKAS in the UK, DAkkS in Germany, JAS-ANZ in Australia)
      Sector experienceDemonstrated experience in packaging waste audits, environmental product declarations, or EPR compliance verification
      IndependenceNo commercial relationship with Block Box (Pty) Ltd or with any named legacy competitor
      Jurisdiction coverageAble to issue a statement recognised in at least one of: United Kingdom, European Union, Australia

      Recommended organisations (not an exhaustive list): Intertek (UK/global), Bureau Veritas (global), SGS (global), TÜV Rheinland (EU/global), DEKRA (EU/global).

      5. Access and Logistics

      Block Box (Pty) Ltd will provide the auditor with:

      1. Full access to the production facility for the duration of the facility visit.
      2. The complete source document set listed in Section 1.2 above.
      3. A sample set of finished cornice units (minimum 5 units, 110 mm profile) for Component C inspection.
      4. Contact details for Isowall Group (EPS block supplier) to verify material specifications directly if required.
      5. The Sunny Packs supplier pricing data (referenced in Market Research Report v2.0 §5.2) as a starting point for legacy benchmark identification.

      For audit scheduling and logistics, contact:
      Heyns Schoeman, Block Box (Pty) Ltd
      (Contact details on file — available on request to qualified auditing organisations)

      6. Intended Use of the Auditor's Statement

      Once issued, the Auditor's Statement (Annex A of the ESG Export Brief) may be:

      • Shared with UK, EU, and Australian procurement departments as supporting evidence for buyer-side EPR, PPWR, and APCO compliance filings.
      • Cited in tender responses to government and institutional buyers operating under green procurement mandates (UK Government Buying Standards, EU Green Public Procurement criteria, Australian Government procurement guidelines).
      • Referenced in any updated version of the BlockBox ESG Export Brief as the source for the waste elimination figures, upgrading their status from "projected" to "independently verified."

      The Auditor's Statement does not constitute an ISO 14001 certification, a Life Cycle Assessment, or a carbon footprint declaration. Those certifications, if required, are separate engagements described in the ESG Export Brief §7.2.

      7. Limitations Acknowledged

      Block Box (Pty) Ltd acknowledges the following limitations of the proposed audit:

      1. Legacy benchmark variability: The waste elimination quantities depend on which specific legacy product and packaging format the auditor selects as the benchmark. Different suppliers use different sleeve lengths and box configurations. The auditor's statement must name the benchmark used so that buyers can assess its comparability to the competitors they deal with.
      2. Single audit point in time: The audit verifies the production process as observed on the audit date. Future changes to the production process or packaging specification would require a revised audit.
      3. No carbon quantification: This audit scope does not cover Scope 1/2/3 emissions or carbon footprint per unit. A separate LCA engagement would be required for that purpose.
      4. EPS recyclability infrastructure: Mono-material confirmation (Component C) confirms technical recyclability potential; it does not verify that EPS recycling infrastructure exists or is used in any specific destination market.

      Document version: 1.0 — 15 July 2026
      Prepared by Block Box (Pty) Ltd for submission to an accredited third-party auditor. This document does not constitute legal advice. Buyers should confirm their own EPR, PPWR, and APCO compliance obligations with qualified legal counsel.

      #66 - Add Product Database Layer (2 m EPS Cornice seed)

      What & Why

      The July 24 database audit confirmed that every SKU price, cost, and packaging figure in the app is AI-generated and hardcoded in the frontend. This task replaces that fiction with owner-verified data by:

      1. Adding a new set of Drizzle/PostgreSQL tables for product data (7 new tables — all 8 existing tables are untouched and keep running normally).
      2. Seeding all 15 verified 2 m EPS cornice SKUs with exact pricing, packaging, and CNC production specs as supplied by the patent owner.
      3. Copying the 15 uploaded product-card images (in attached_assets/) to a server-side asset path (NOT public/) so they serve through the authenticated API.
      4. Adding owner-only API endpoints to read and (later) update product data.
      5. Replacing every hardcoded SKU/pricing/packaging value in the Factory Workspace, Licensee Workspace, and Quote Calculator with live database queries.

      The 1.5 m BlockBox cornice family (raw material cost → CNC dilution → tiered pricing) is a separate follow-up task once the owner provides that data. The schema is designed to accommodate it without any structural change.

      Database schema (new tables only — existing 8 tables untouched)

      product_families

      One row per product category. Columns: id (uuid pk), code (text unique — e.g. EPS_2M, BLOCKBOX_1500), name, description, is_active (bool), sort_order (int), created_at, updated_at.

      sku_profiles

      One row per profile (15 rows seeded for 2 m range). Columns: id (uuid pk), family_id (fk → product_families), sku_code (text unique), profile_name, length_mm (int), width_mm (int), dim_height_mm (int), dim_depth_mm (int), is_active (bool), sort_order (int), created_at, updated_at.

      sku_pricing

      Base catalog prices per SKU (owner-verified, not AI-generated). Columns: id (uuid pk), sku_id (fk → sku_profiles), currency (text, default ZAR), price_per_piece (numeric), price_per_5pack (numeric), price_per_carton (numeric), effective_from (date), notes (text), created_at, updated_at. (Tiered wholesale pricing T1/T2/T3 added in follow-up task.)

      sku_packaging

      Carton and pack specs per SKU. Columns: id (uuid pk), sku_id (fk → sku_profiles), pcs_per_5pack (int), pcs_per_carton (int), moq_5packs (int), carton_length_mm (int), carton_width_mm (int), carton_height_mm (int), carton_weight_kg (numeric), carton_cbm (numeric), created_at, updated_at.

      sku_production_specs

      CNC cutting production matrix per SKU. Columns: id (uuid pk), sku_id (fk → sku_profiles), eps_block_length_mm (int), eps_block_width_mm (int), eps_block_height_mm (int), wire_count (int), wire_spacing_mm (int), layers_per_block (int), pcs_per_block (int), heat_clearance_mm (int default 10), feedrate_mm_per_min (int), variac_low (int), variac_high (int), machine_steps_per_mm (numeric), created_at, updated_at.

      sku_images

      One or more images per SKU (product card, render, etc.). Columns: id (uuid pk), sku_id (fk → sku_profiles), image_type (text — product_card | render | photo), file_path (text — server-side path, never public/), mime_type (text), sort_order (int), created_at.

      sku_raw_material_costs

      Raw block cost per SKU family (to be filled for 1.5 m once owner provides ZAR cost). Columns: id (uuid pk), sku_id (fk → sku_profiles), block_cost_zar (numeric nullable), supplier_name (text nullable), cost_per_piece_zar (numeric — computed: block_cost / pcs_per_block), effective_from (date), notes (text), created_at, updated_at.

      Done looks like

      • Running SELECT * FROM sku_profiles returns all 15 2 m profiles with correct SKU codes, dimensions, and pricing — zero hardcoded values remain in the frontend files.
      • The Factory Workspace, Licensee Workspace, and Quote Calculator all display values pulled live from the database (no page-refresh required to pick up a price change).
      • Hitting GET /api/products/skus (owner/admin auth required) returns the full catalogue JSON with pricing and packaging.
      • Product card images are served through GET /api/products/skus/:id/image (auth gated) — they cannot be accessed via a direct public URL.
      • All 8 existing tables (user_access_allowlist, nda_acceptances, contacts, email_log, partner_requests, payments, activity_logs, user_sessions) continue to operate and grow without any change.
